known_from_text.basis: Verses 1–2 speak of the earth and its fullness belonging to Yahweh because he founded and established it over waters.
known_from_text.claim: The psalm declares Yahweh's ownership of the earth and relates it to his founding of the world.

known_from_text.basis: Verses 3–4 ask who may ascend and stand there, then describe clean hands, a pure heart, and avoidance of falsehood and deceitful oaths.
known_from_text.claim: Approach to Yahweh's holy place is associated with moral integrity.

known_from_text.basis: Verses 8 and 10 answer the question about the king with descriptions of Yahweh, culminating in Yahweh of hosts.
known_from_text.claim: The closing exchange identifies the king of glory with Yahweh.

known_from_text.basis: The supplied arrangement marks lines B, C, and B,C and labels a section 'CALL AND RESPONSE.'
known_from_text.claim: The setting uses alternating and combined voices.

known_from_text.basis: Examples in the full arrangement include fire at the holy place, holy thunder, and the petition 'draw us nearer.'
known_from_text.claim: The setting introduces imagery and petitions beyond the Hebrew.

not_known_from_text.why_not: The traditional heading associates the psalm with David but does not independently establish authorship.

not_known_from_text.claim: The psalm was written for a particular historical event or festival.
not_known_from_text.why_not: Neither the heading nor the psalm's imagery names an occasion.

not_known_from_text.claim: The gate exchange records an actual procession or prescribes its performance.
not_known_from_text.why_not: The dialogue and entrance imagery are compatible with worship but do not document a specific performance.

not_known_from_text.claim: The imported English reproduces or adapts a particular identifiable published translation.
not_known_from_text.why_not: The supplied comparisons share the psalm's underlying content but do not establish a distinctive verbal source for this setting; its provenance is not supplied.

guardrails.cultic_setting: The mountain of Yahweh, holy place, questions about who may enter, and summons to gates suggest worship and an entrance setting. The text does not establish a particular historical procession, festival, temple ceremony, or performance.
guardrails.heading_attribution: The Hebrew heading identifies the composition as a psalm associated with David. The expression is traditionally read as 'of David,' but the heading alone does not establish that David wrote it or identify the circumstances of composition. The English lyric does not sing the heading.

analyses.method: The architectural analysis compares the supplied Hebrew and English verse assignments, then uses the full pasted arrangement to identify section labels, repetitions, and performance apparatus. The compact literal sense is based on the supplied Hebrew and token glosses, with visible token/gloss inconsistencies resolved against the Hebrew itself. Translation similarities were checked against the three supplied English texts; no external edition or lexicon was consulted.

analyses.summary: The setting moves from Yahweh's ownership and founding of the earth to questions about approach to his holy place, an account of the seekers, and a repeated welcome for the king. Its lyric expands the psalm's images and turns the final exchange into a dramatic call and response. The full arrangement returns to the gate chorus and closes by recalling its opening. All ten verses were imported from an existing setting, but its author or published source cannot be identified from the supplied evidence; no particular translation can be named as one it reproduces or adapts.

arrangements.title: Psalm 24

lines.rationale: The English places the psalm before its attribution to David.

lines.text: The earth is Yahweh’s, and all that fills it,
The world and all who dwell within.
For he has founded it upon the seas,
And on the rivers made it firm.
Who shall ascend the hill of Yahweh?
Who in his holy place shall stand?

lines.rationale: Heart and hands exchange their Hebrew order for the sung line.
lines.text: The one whose heart is pure, whose hands are clean,
Who lifts not my soul to what is false,
And swears no oath with words of deceit.
That one receives blessing from Yahweh,

lines.rationale: The line renders the God of his salvation as the God who saves, leaving the possessive implicit.
lines.text: And righteousness from the God who saves.

lines.rationale: The repeated seeking represented by the textual forms is folded into one phrase.
lines.text: This is the generation seeking him,
Who seek your face, O Jacob.
Lift up your heads, O gates!
Be lifted up, you ancient doors,
That the King of glory may come in.
Who is this King of glory?
Lift up your heads, O gates!
Be lifted up, you ancient doors,
That the King of glory may come in.
Who is this King of glory?
Yahweh of hosts, he is the King of glory.

arrangements.guidance:
Keep the language, imagery and form of the earlier Bone and Ash setting of this psalm, given below: its wording, its B / C call and response, its sections and their musical directions, and phrases such as "the radiant King", "you old stone doorways", "Lift your crowns, you gates of age", "Hands unbloodied, hearts undivided", "where his fire dwells", "Yahweh, ready for the war", "the blaze before us", "the Lord victorious". Expanding or compressing the Hebrew's images is welcome.

Do not invent lines for cadence. Every sung line must render words of the Hebrew. The earlier setting's lines that rendered nothing in the Hebrew are marked "left out" below and must not come back in any form. Where leaving one out breaks a sentence ("every breath here", "God of Jacob,", the third "Who is he,"), finish it from that verse's own Hebrew or rework the lines around it, without adding a line the Hebrew does not have. Put musical directions in section labels, not in lines.

Sing Selah where the Hebrew has it: after 24:6 (end of the pre-chorus) and after 24:10.

The earlier setting:

[INTRO - 4 bars: piano in 6/8, ascending motif, soft guitar swells]
[VERSE 1 - quiet, awestruck]
   B: All ground beneath us / belongs to Yahweh; / every breath here
   (left out: moves in his hand.)
   B: Every nation, / every creature, / all who wake / on sea and land.
   B: He laid its pillars / over deep waters; / he drew its borders / above the flood.
   B: He made it steady,
   (left out: he made it singing, / held together / by his word.)
[VERSE 2 - searching, rhythmic]
   B: Who can go up / to his high mountain? / Who can remain / where his fire dwells?
   B: Hands unbloodied, / hearts undivided,
   (left out: lips that do not / trade in spells.)
   B: No soul given / over to nothing, / no oath fastened / to a lie.
   B: Such a one will / carry blessing, / vindicated / by God Most High.
[PRE-CHORUS - lift]
   B: This is the generation / running after him; / C: running after him.
   B: These are the ones / who are seeking your face; / C: seeking your face.
   B: God of Jacob,
   (left out: draw us nearer; / C: draw us nearer.)
[INSTRUMENTAL TURN - 2 bars: guitar echoes the vocal melody]
[CHORUS 1 - strong, rising]
   B,C: Open wide, / you old stone doorways! / B,C: Lift your crowns, / you gates of age! / B,C: Make the road / for heaven's ruler! / B,C: Let the radiant King / come in!
[CALL AND RESPONSE - half-time feel]
   B: Who comes clothed / in burning honor? / C: Yahweh, mighty. / C: Yahweh, fearless.
   B: Who comes crowned / with holy thunder? / C: Yahweh, ready / for the war.
[CHORUS 2 - bigger: Chorus 1 sung again]
[BRIDGE - dramatic, building]
   B: Who is he, / the blaze before us? / C: Yahweh of hosts.
   B: Who is he, / the Lord victorious? / C: Yahweh of hosts.
   B: Who is he,
   (left out: the song of heaven?)
   C: Yahweh of hosts.
   B,C: He is the radiant King. / B,C: He is the radiant King.
[FINAL CHORUS - full band, triumphant: Chorus 1 sung again, then]
   B,C: Yahweh of hosts, / the Lord victorious; / B,C: Yahweh of hosts, / the radiant King. (twice)
[OUTRO - repeat softer, then final hit]
   B: All ground beneath us / belongs to Yahweh. / C: Every breath here
   (left out: moves in his hand.)
